teacher_review_theme: Conservation of mass behind continuity
scientific_scope_teacher_note: The source B correctly identifies mass conservation. The official B-38 target uses Application to justify the relationship; mere recognition is a Knowledge-level prerequisite rather than automatically a certified B-38 application item.

teacher_review_theme: General two-section relation assumes steady single-throughflow without sources or storage
scientific_scope_teacher_note: The source B ρ₁A₁v₁=ρ₂A₂v₂ is steady mass conservation for one inlet, one outlet, no accumulating mass, and mean normal speeds. It is not universal for pipes with leaks, storage, branching or unsteady flow; retain the intended simplified assumptions.

teacher_review_theme: Incompressible continuity equation
scientific_scope_teacher_note: A₁v₁=A₂v₂ follows by canceling equal densities in steady one-inlet/one-outlet flow without accumulation or leak; option C is the original scientifically supported result.

teacher_review_theme: Area is perpendicular to mean flow
scientific_scope_teacher_note: A denotes the flow cross-section normal to mean motion, rather than wetted outside surface or graph area. This is foundational symbol identification not in itself an Application-level question.

teacher_review_theme: Flow-rate speed is cross-sectional average normal component
scientific_scope_teacher_note: The source A is scientifically right when v denotes mean normal speed across section: Q=Av. Nonuniform real profiles require integration of local normal velocity or its cross-sectional average, not an arbitrary point speed.

teacher_review_theme: Unit of Av versus B-36 Application
scientific_scope_teacher_note: [Av]=m²·m/s=m³/s, correct C; however this is dimensional recall/knowledge, not automatically a direct application of the continuity equation meeting the official B-36 cognitive demand. Keep as prerequisite practice.

teacher_review_theme: Mass flow rate and ρAv
scientific_scope_teacher_note: ρAv equals mass/time for representative section average flow, assuming density uniform or appropriately averaged. Option C is right, but the item recognizes a formula rather than proving the conservation law.

teacher_review_theme: kg/s is foundational mass-rate knowledge
scientific_scope_teacher_note: The correct source option C is kg s⁻¹ for mass flow rate. This is a definition/unit recall question; the official B-38 summative target requires justification/application, so do not automatically certify cognitive alignment.

teacher_review_theme: Displacement formula is supporting kinematics rather than direct continuity
scientific_scope_teacher_note: Δx=vΔt for constant speed/velocity along a straight segment is correct option B, but does not alone test B-36's continuity-problem application. It is a step in the derivation and should remain supportive practice until teacher SLO review.

teacher_review_theme: Flow volume in time interval
scientific_scope_teacher_note: A fluid slug length vΔt passing area A gives ΔV=AvΔt; v must be the mean normal component or simple uniform-flow approximation. The dimensions are m³.

teacher_review_theme: Mass from swept volume
scientific_scope_teacher_note: Δm=ρAvΔt follows from ρΔV, using the appropriate density for the section and mean normal speed; candidate B-38 mass-conservation support only, no item-level approval yet.

teacher_review_theme: Equality of densities for incompressible flow
scientific_scope_teacher_note: Source C properly cancels ρ₁ and ρ₂ when they are equal in the intended flow. Equal pressures or equal areas are not necessary conditions for density cancellation.

teacher_review_theme: Volumetric discharge interpretation
scientific_scope_teacher_note: Q=Av means volume throughput per time with units m³/s in an ideal steady flow through a section. Recognizing the meaning is foundational, not individually certified as an Application-level B-36 question.

teacher_review_theme: Figure 6.7 printed NBF attribution without attached figure
scientific_scope_teacher_note: The teacher-prepared master states Fig.6.7 is a one-inlet/one-outlet pipe, so the prepared key A is internally consistent, but the original printed NBF Fig.6.7 panel/caption on pp.96–99 was NOT reopened. GitHub Q14 contains a figure reference in the stem but no source figure-link field; verify original figure and student readability before any certified source-figure use.

teacher_review_theme: Conserved Q when flow is unbranched and steady
scientific_scope_teacher_note: Source D follows from incompressible steady flow with no source/sink or storage. It does not require pressure, area, or speed to remain separately constant along the whole pipe.

teacher_review_theme: Inverse area-speed proportionality at fixed discharge
scientific_scope_teacher_note: v=Q/A is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area only for unchanged volumetric discharge along steady incompressible unbranched pipe. Option D is correct under those stated conditions.

teacher_review_theme: Inflow mass equals outflow mass in steady condition
scientific_scope_teacher_note: The equality of mass passing sections in the same Δt follows from steady continuity without leaks or accumulation; source C correct and better aligned with B-38 reasoning than a formula-only item.

teacher_review_theme: Density SI units and B-38 Application classification
scientific_scope_teacher_note: ρ has SI unit kg m⁻³, so source B is correct. Unit identification does not by itself justify mass continuity as required by official B-38 Application; keep as a study prerequisite and withhold per-item certification.

teacher_review_theme: Equal flow area implies equal average speed
scientific_scope_teacher_note: When A₁=A₂>0 in an unbranched steady incompressible flow with fixed Q, v₁=v₂; absolute velocity direction can change around bends, but mean speed magnitudes agree in the intended problem.

teacher_review_theme: Branch continuity and signed rate accounting
scientific_scope_teacher_note: For steady incompressible one-inlet/two-outlet division, Q_main=Q_branch1+Q_branch2 when positive magnitudes refer to their own outward/inward directions. More generally signed fluxes sum to zero with consistent normals; option B says all directions taken positive and is invalid. Source C is correct.
